name: Pokerize
description: Pokerize is a rummy variant in which play follows basic draw-and-discard rummy (draw one, meld sets or runs, lay off on melds, discard one) and the result or scoring is interpreted using standard poker hand rankings (high card, pair, two pair, flush, full house, etc.).

overview.description: Pokerize is a rummy variant in which play follows basic draw-and-discard rummy (draw one, meld sets or runs, lay off on melds, discard one) and the result or scoring is interpreted using standard poker hand rankings (high card, pair, two pair, flush, full house, etc.).

history.origins: Rummy games derive from early 20th century; theories point to Mexican Conquian or Asian origins. Pokerize applies poker hand rankings to rummy outcomes, combining rummy melding with poker-style evaluation.
timeline: Mid 20th century: Variants that score or rank hands in poker style appear.
history.cultural: Played as a rummy variant in casual and home settings where players enjoy both melding and poker-style hand comparison.
history.evolution: Pokerize extends basic rummy by evaluating hands or scores using standard poker hand hierarchy instead of or in addition to deadwood points.

setup.dealing: Deal 10 cards each for 2 players, 7 for 3–4 players, or 6 for 5–6 players, one at a time. Remaining cards form the stock; turn one card face up to start the discard pile.
setup.equipment: One standard deck; score sheet if playing to a target score.

rules.objective: Dispose of all cards by melding and discarding; when a hand ends, outcome or scoring is determined using standard poker hand rankings (e.g. best five-card poker hand from melds or deadwood).
rules.gameplay: 1. Draw one card from the stock or the top of the discard pile. 2. Optionally meld sets (3–4 of a rank) or runs (3+ consecutive same suit). 3. Optionally lay off cards on existing melds. 4. Discard one card face up to end your turn. 5. First to empty their hand ends the hand; hands are then evaluated or scored using poker hand rankings.
keyRules: Melds are sets (3–4 of a rank) or runs (3+ in suit).
Lay off is allowed on any meld on the table.
One draw and one discard per turn.
Poker hand rankings (high card through straight flush) determine scoring or winner when applied to the hand result.

strategy.basic: Prioritize building toward strong poker hands in melds; keep flexible runs; discard high deadwood.
strategy.intermediate: Track discards; balance melding early versus holding for better poker-hand combinations; lay off to block opponents when useful.
strategy.advanced: Model opponent melds and optimize for best five-card poker hand from your melds and deadwood at hand end.
tips: Poker hand ranking applies at show-down; structure melds to maximize your best five cards.
Rummy tactics (runs, sets) still apply; add poker hand evaluation when going out or scoring.

variations.name: Deadwood as poker hand
variations.description: Only unmelded cards are evaluated as a poker hand; highest poker hand among deadwood wins or scores.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes which cards are evaluated as poker hand; no engine constants to override.

scoring.description: When a player goes out, hands are evaluated using standard poker hand rankings (high card, pair, two pair, flush, full house, etc.); winner or scores determined by agreed variant (e.g. best poker hand from melds or deadwood).
scoring.winCondition: First to reach agreed target score or win the most hands; each hand outcome determined by poker hand ranking.

synthesis.shortDescription: Rummy variant: draw one, meld sets and runs, lay off, discard one; outcome or scoring uses standard poker hand rankings.
